message.reasoning:
We need to analyze method getGrossProfit(Num finalPrice). Identify all possible exception scenarios. Look at code:

```
public Num getGrossProfit(Num finalPrice) {
    Num grossProfit;
    if (isOpened()) {
        grossProfit = entry.getAmount().multipliedBy(finalPrice).minus(entry.getValue());
    } else {
        grossProfit = exit.getValue().minus(entry.getValue());
    }
    // Profits of long position are losses of short
    if (entry.isSell()) {
        grossProfit = grossProfit.negate();
    }
    return grossProfit;
}
```

Potential null pointers: entry could be null, exit could be null, finalPrice could be null. Also entry.getAmount() could be null, entry.getValue() could be null, exit.getValue() could be null. Also entry.isSell() could be null? isSell returns boolean, likely not null.

If isOpened() true means exit is null, but entry must not be null. If entry null -> NPE. If finalPrice null -> NPE when multiplied. If entry.getAmount() null -> NPE. If entry.getValue() null -> NPE. If isOpened false (closed) and exit null -> NPE. Also entry null in closed case also NPE.

Thus exception scenarios: NullPointerException for null entry, null exit, null finalPrice, null amount, null value.

Also maybe IllegalArgumentException if finalPrice is NaN? But code uses NaN as Num; not exception.

Thus we need test cases that trigger each exception.

We need to follow existing test case structure, avoid duplication. Existing tests cover many scenarios but not nulls.

So we create new groups: "Null entry trade", "Null exit trade on closed position", "Null finalPrice on opened position", "Null amount in entry", "Null entry value", "Null exit value". Also maybe combination.

But Position class may not allow setting directly; but for test we can use reflection or a constructor? Not given. Assume we can set via constructor or setter for test. We'll just describe scenario.

Each case: input finalPrice value (could be DecimalNum.valueOf(5) or null). Expected exception: NullPointerException.
